findings.title: Git commands used for the clean-source gate run with the unsanitized environment
findings.message: The git calls in source_state and source_files inherit the caller's full environment, while the Go calls use the allowlisted child_environment(). Variables such as GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE (set when the script runs from a git hook or wrapper) or GIT_CONFIG_* can point git at a different repository or index. The public-release "clean" gate, the recorded commit and the tracked-file list could then be wrong. That undermines the "committed and clean" guarantee and the before/after consistency check. The git calls also have no timeout.
findings.suggestion: Run every git invocation with a sanitized environment: drop GIT_* variables, or pass `--git-dir=<root>/.git` explicitly. Add a `timeout=COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to each call, and reuse one helper for all git calls.

findings.title: Allowlist passes proxy credentials and desktop-session variables to all archive-code child processes
findings.message: A single allowlist is used for every child process, including checks that run archived, possibly self-attested code. Proxy variables often embed credentials (http://user:pass@host). DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS expose the user's desktop session, though the spec says default checks create no native windows. The documented claim that unrelated secrets are dropped is weakened, because these credential-bearing and session-access variables reach every child.
findings.suggestion: Split the allowlist: a base set for Go build/test/vet, and a display/GPU set added only for the `--runtime` launch. Also document, or strip, proxy credentials. For example, make `child_environment(runtime=False)` include the display/D-Bus/GPU variables only when `runtime=True`.
